params_note: dense model; the checkpoint includes the pixtral vision tower + projector (0.439 B); text decoder + embeddings + lm_head = 23.572 B
weights_gb_note: decimal GB; bf16 = 2 x params (= sum of the HF-format safetensors shards); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate (0.5159 B per quantisable decoder-layer linear weight, rest in bf16)
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: 48.0 GB weights incl. a 0.9 GB pixtral vision tower; long [THINK] generations need KV cache (0.16 MB/token)

hidden_last_80gb.verdict: fits: no hidden_last chunk of the hard / wmdp / nonbio direction pools exceeds the free memory of an 80 GB card (a prompt above max_tokens_per_chunk tokens would).
hidden_last_80gb.basis: ESTIMATE from config numbers, not a GPU measurement. sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True): per prompt token the hidden states of all layers ((num_layers+1) * hidden_size * 2 B), the full-sequence logits (vocab_size * 2 B) and, only if the model config has use_cache=true (forward(use_cache=None) then builds a cache; kv_cache_alive says so, and all OLMo configs ship use_cache=false), the KV cache (2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * 2 B; an upper bound for sliding-window layers) are alive at once, and bytes_per_prompt_token is their sum. core.batches() budgets KV, prefill attention and a 14000-token chunk but not this cost. free_gib_after_weights = 79.2 GiB (an 80 GB card) - 0.8 GiB (CUDA context) - bf16 weights. max_tokens_per_chunk = free / bytes_per_prompt_token: a chunk of b prompts padded to length p holds b*p tokens, and a single prompt above the limit cannot be processed at all. hard_pool_measured: core.batches(max_new=0, cap=16, free) over the direction-pool prompts evals.get_pool()['hard'] under framings N and E with this adapter and the real tokenizer; chunks_over_budget counts chunks whose estimated peak exceeds the free memory. Measured 2026-11-22; the pool follows sbx/evals.py (n_prompts and max_prompt_chars identify it).

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (huggingface_hub.get_hf_file_metadata) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (200 = accessible, 401/403 raise)

min_transformers_note: same as mistral-small-3.2-24b: Mistral3Model wrapper (model.model.language_model.layers) first appears in 4.52.0

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_config(real hub config) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device); numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class through sbx.core.Ctx (sbx/tests/test_adapters_misc.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)

checkpoint_key_check.method: keys of model.safetensors.index.json (after the class's _checkpoint_conversion_mapping) vs meta-device state_dict, transformers 4.57.6

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions) with the real tokenizer + adapter.build; long-context sets (labbench) are much longer

prompt_tokens_by_set.basis: framing N, real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/hard/*.jsonl, data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl, data/wmdp_train.jsonl; n_over_context counts prompts with prompt_tokens + max_new > context_window

est_tokens_per_question_basis: estimate: long [THINK] traces on MCQ (vendor max_new_tokens 131072); NOT measured. Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run; outputs longer than max_new are truncated and count as unparsed.
template_notes: Mistral-Small-3.2 architecture/format (tekken V7 string built by hand: <s>[SYSTEM_PROMPT]{sys}[/SYSTEM_PROMPT][INST]{user}[/INST]) trained to reason inside [THINK]..[/THINK]. The repo has NO HF tokenizer/template (tekken.json only); the Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning HF tokenizer is used: its vocab is identical to Magistral's tekken.json (0 mismatching ranks of 130,072) and it has real [THINK]/[/THINK] special tokens (ids 34/35, same ids as in Magistral's tekken v13). The vendor SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt ('# HOW YOU SHOULD THINK AND ANSWER ... [THINK]..[/THINK]') is the always-present default system prompt (it switches thinking on; framing text is appended after a blank line, never replacing it). The model emits [THINK] itself; split() cuts at [/THINK]; text with [THINK] but no [/THINK] is truncated reasoning (final ''). Design choice: framing text is APPENDED to the model's default system prompt (default + blank line + framing), so N-vs-framing contrasts differ only by the framing paragraph; set the class attribute adapter.keep_default_system = False to get the vendor template's native semantics (framing REPLACES the default system prompt; N is unchanged).
known_issues: Vendor sampling: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, up to 131072 new tokens. sbx decodes greedily; the vendor recommends sampling for this model, and greedy decoding of long-CoT models is prone to repetition loops -> look at the parse rate / truncation rate of baseline N before reading any steering effect.
max_new=4096 truncates long traces (unparsed = wrong); compare parse rates across conditions.
Borrowed tokenizer (Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning HF repo, loads fine with transformers 4.57.6) -> adapter.tokenizer_repos documents it; load() checks len(tok) == model text vocab size.
Text path of Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration (layers at model.model.language_model.layers, transformers>=4.52); verified like mistral-small-3.2-24b (same config; only the weights differ).
Repo holds consolidated.safetensors + HF shards; from_pretrained fetches only the HF shards (48 GB).
Output format on the real model is UNVERIFIED; est_tokens_per_question is an estimate.
recommended_gpu: 1x 80 GB (A100/H100); batches are KV-limited for 4k-token generations
greedy_only_note: sbx decodes greedily; the vendor recommends sampling for this model, and greedy decoding of long-CoT models is prone to repetition loops -> look at the parse rate / truncation rate of baseline N before reading any steering effect.
tokenizer_repo_note: borrowed HF tokenizer (identical vocab, real [THINK] tokens); see template_notes
